title: Photography
description: Photographic cinematography treats the movie as a print: a single decisive frame, posed or found light, often Centered Composition or Tableau blocking, with the camera pretending it could hang on a wall. Motion is allowed, but the still is the law.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Hold. This is the picture.
A candlelit room is arranged like a painting. A river still is exposed for the sky.
People occupy the frame as if a shutter, not a scene, were about to close. It is close to Arthouse patience but not the same.
Arthouse may be empty, slightly ugly, and long. Photography wants the print: a chosen moment, shaped light, a composition that would survive without time.
If the camera hunts, you have left the still.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Tripod. One frame.
Pose the bodies or wait for a still gesture. Light as a stills photographer would: window, candle, or a single shaped key, not a moving TV-style fill.
35mm to 85mm, sometimes a zoom used as a stills crop (as in Barry Lyndon). Prompt still-photography grammar, a single decisive frame, posed light, the movie pretending to be a print.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the beat is a picture, not a passage. Do not use it for coverage that must cut, or for empty duration that refuses to compose.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Photography is the print as grammar. Tableau is staged group composition.
Centered Composition is a placement rule. Arthouse may refuse the decisive moment.
Static Locked-Off is only the locked head. A photographically lit moving shot can still be this look if every frame could hang.
A locked empty hold with odd headroom is arthouse first.
TableauHold the arrangement.
Centered CompositionControl, ritual, comedy, or fate.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Arthouse emptiness or a moving coverage scene: odd unused air, or a walk-and-talk. The tell is a frame that would not survive as a still, or a camera that hunts.
Fix: lock, compose as a print, and shape one light.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Photography in film?
A look that treats motion pictures as prints: decisive framing, posed or found stills light, often tableau or centered, with the camera behaving like a shutter rather than like coverage.
Photography vs Arthouse

Both may lock the camera. Arthouse uses duration and empty air, even if the still is imperfect. Photography wants a picture that could hang: posed light, a chosen moment. One waits. The other composes.
When should I use Photography?
When the beat is a still: a portrait, a landscape plate, a candlelit tableau. Skip it for hunting vérité, for jump-cut streets, or for empty holds that refuse to compose.
How do I prompt Photography for AI image or video?
Write: Still-photography grammar on [Subject], a single decisive frame, posed light, tripod, the movie pretending to be a print. Name the print type. Do not add a hunting camera.
